newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down across the board on Monday on heavy profit-taking, although some speculative buying emerged in the afternoon session, pushing prices off their lows, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,370 yuan ($2,817) per tonne, losing 50 yuan. It opened at 23,250 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,200 and a high of 23,400.
March fell 80 yuan to 23,200, April 80 to 23,300, May 90 to 23,340, July 90 to 23,360 and August 180 to 23,320.
Combined volume fell to 39,210 tonnes from 40,090.
Copper opened lower on profit-taking triggered by Friday's losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), but some speculative buying pushed prices up towards the close.
Traders said many investors remained on the sidelines because they were uncertain about the short-term market direction.
"Most institutions do not dare to build large positions due to market uncertainties," one trader said. "Retail investors dominated today's market.
Traders said LME would continue to be a major factor on Shanghai copper's movements in the short term.
Analysts said they expected copper to consolidate around the current levels in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down in slow trading. March fell 80 yuan to 15,920 per tonne, April 80 to 16,250 and May 20 to 16,580.
Combined volume fell to 610 tonnes from 2,150.
